pairs.question: Quid igitur, si intra annum quidem decesserit, condicio autem heredi adscripta post annum extiterit? an quasi militis testamentum valeat?
pairs.derivation: Author poses the case (a soldier dies within the year but the heir's condition matures after the year) and asks 'an quasi militis testamentum valeat?'. The reply is 'et placet, valere quasi militis.' I dropped the framing connective 'et' and the assertion-verb is kept as 'Placet' (the verdict), normalizing capitalization; answer ends at the full stop. Next sentence ('Sed et si quis ante militiam...') moves to a different case.

pairs.question: Si pars aliqua vacet nec tamen quisquam sine parte heres institutus sit, quid iuris sit?
pairs.answer: Vacantem partem singulis tacite pro hereditaria parte accedere et perinde haberi ac si ex tertiis partibus heredes scripti essent.
pairs.derivation: Author asks 'quid iuris sit?' after the framing 'Videamus' (let us see), which I dropped, normalizing capitalization. The example 'veluti si tres ex quartis partibus heredes scripti sunt' is illustration, not part of the answer. The answer is the indirect statement introduced by framing 'et constat', which I dropped, keeping 'vacantem partem... scripti essent'. Window ends at the colon/first stop; the reply then turns to the opposite case ('et ex diverso si plus asse in portionibus sit...').

pairs.question: An servo heredis recte legamus?
pairs.answer: Pure inutiliter legari, nec quidquam proficere si vivo testatore de potestate heredis exierit, quia quod inutile foret legatum, si statim post factum testamentum decessisset testator, hoc non debet ideo valere, quia diutius testator vixerit.
pairs.derivation: Question 'An servo heredis recte legamus' is framed by the speech-verb 'quaeritur' ('it is asked'), which I dropped, normalizing to an interrogative. Answer follows framing 'et constat' (dropped); the operative answer 'pure inutiliter legari' plus its reason runs contiguously to the first full stop ('...vixerit'). The next sentence ('sub condicione vero recte legatur...') treats the conditional-bequest case separately.
